## Trial `kernel-network-hardening-ubuntu1__GD7Vgz6`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor persistently disabled ICMP redirect acceptance and source-routed packet acceptance for IPv4 on node1 via /etc/sysctl.d/60-icmp-redirect-hardening.conf, applied it at runtime, and — going beyond the minimum — validated true persistence with an actual reboot showing a changed boot identity and intact hardening values afterward. All material outcomes are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence, and the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was executed cleanly and without unnecessary mutations.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.950 | 0.920 | 10/2 |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **R1 — Satisfied:** Persistently disable acceptance of ICMP redirects (net.ipv4.conf.all/default.accept_redirects) on node1
  - **Why:** Baseline showed accept_redirects=1 for all/default. Executor wrote /etc/sysctl.d/60-icmp-redirect-hardening.conf setting accept_redirects (and secure_redirects) to 0 for all/default, applied via sysctl --system with no later file overriding it, and confirmed runtime values were 0. Kernel combines conf.all and per-interface accept_redirects with AND logic, so setting conf.all=0 disables acceptance network-wide even though per-interface (ens2, lo) values remained 1 — this matches standard hardening practice (e.g. CIS benchmarks) of only setting all/default. Persistence was directly verified: node1 was rebooted (boot_id changed f19de998...→80fe4256..., uptime reset to 7s), and post-reboot the six sysctl values and the config file content were re-checked and confirmed intact without manual reapplication.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-ec239edde8dc49f0`, `cmd-4bf62110ac934b64`, `cmd-86b46bd523e249aa`, `cmd-ef4c40b6ce9e4bc6`, `cmd-a09da45b81ae424e`, `cmd-0605b02868c840d6`, `cmd-939c089d61ee4763`, `cmd-34490d7524744010`
- **R2 — Satisfied:** Persistently disable acceptance of source-routed packets (net.ipv4.conf.all/default.accept_source_route) on node1
  - **Why:** Baseline showed accept_source_route=0 (all) / 1 (default), i.e. inconsistent/partially open. The same sysctl.d file set accept_source_route=0 for both all and default, applied and verified at runtime (all/default = 0). accept_source_route also uses kernel AND-logic between conf.all and per-interface, so the all=0 setting disables it network-wide. Post-reboot verification confirmed both values remained 0 and the config file was intact, demonstrating persistence.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-ec239edde8dc49f0`, `cmd-4bf62110ac934b64`, `cmd-ef4c40b6ce9e4bc6`, `cmd-939c089d61ee4763`, `cmd-34490d7524744010`
- **R3 — Satisfied:** Configuration survives an actual reboot (persistence, not just runtime sysctl -w)
  - **Why:** Executor captured pre-restart boot_id/uptime (f19de998..., 50s), triggered `shutdown -r now` with acknowledgement returned before disconnect, observed connection refused confirming the node went down, polled until SSH was reachable again, confirmed a new boot_id (80fe4256..., uptime 7s) proving an actual reboot occurred (not a service restart), and re-verified all six hardening sysctl values plus the on-disk config file remained correct post-reboot with no manual reapplication. This directly satisfies the bounded disruption + recovery evidence bar for a persistence-related outcome.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-a09da45b81ae424e`, `cmd-0605b02868c840d6`, `cmd-2c8c6ebbc31f4a4e`, `cmd-9f0dfa8f7b8d4464`, `cmd-939c089d61ee4763`, `cmd-34490d7524744010`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`

### Comments and limitations

- Per-interface (non-all/default) sysctl values for ens2 and lo remained 1 after hardening; correctness of network-wide enforcement relies on kernel AND-logic between conf.all and per-interface settings for accept_redirects/accept_source_route, which is standard but was not independently proven with live traffic/packet tests in the evidence.
- No explicit full health check (services, connectivity) was captured immediately pre-restart beyond boot_id/uptime/sysctl state, though this is a low-risk, well-scoped gap given the reboot outcome itself was successfully observed.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.950); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.920; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
